input: n is a nonnegative integer. paths describes a simple undirected graph on garden IDs 1 through n, with no self-loops, no duplicate edges and degree at most three at every vertex. Every path is a two-element array of valid IDs. Let E be the number of paths. All input collections are ordinary finite dense arrays/lists, not subclasses, proxies, sparse arrays or accessor-backed collections; node fields, where present, are plain data fields. Strings are ordinary/primitive strings. There is no concurrent mutation or monkey-patching of standard built-ins. Every individual collection length, computed storage count and index fits [0, 4294967295], except explicit -1 sentinels. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Actual allocation/resource capacity and completion remain qualification obligations, not guarantees from these declared bounds. Python integers are plain int values, excluding bool; node identity keys, when used, are opaque id values.
return: A fresh length-n integer array with colors in {1, 2, 3, 4}, differing at each edge endpoint. The deterministic choice is the smallest currently unused color when gardens are processed in increasing ID order.
mutation_aliasing: Inputs and every edge row remain unchanged. New adjacency rows and output array are independent of the caller; the Solution object retains no state.
numeric: Vertex conversions use exact subtraction by one. Zero denotes uncolored vertices only internally. Degree at most three guarantees at least one of four positive colors is free. All integer inputs and computed mathematical counts (apart from opaque Python identity keys) remain within [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991]. No bitwise coercion is used.
complexity: O(n + E + 1) time and O(n + E + 1) auxiliary/output space. Two adjacency entries per edge are fully counted; the constant-size used array is reallocated for each vertex. Bounds use bounded-word arithmetic, constant-time array indexing and amortized append/pop; output and built-in allocation costs are included.
